LESSON: ROCKS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GEOGRAPHY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Natural Systems and Processes
Topic 2.1: Rocks
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 19

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Rocks, part of Natural Systems and Processes in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 GEOGRAPHY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why are there different types of rocks? 2. How can rocks be classified?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. examine the classification of rocks according to the mode of formation and age,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rocks in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. describe the distribution of rocks in Kenya,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rocks in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. analyse the significance of rocks in Kenya,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rocks in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. sample rock types in your locality,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rocks in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate the significance of rocks in Kenya.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rocks in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. examine the classification of rocks according to the mode of formation and age,

   Rocks helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. describe the distribution of rocks in Kenya,

   Rocks helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. analyse the significance of rocks in Kenya,

   Rocks helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. sample rock types in your locality,

   Rocks helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. appreciate the significance of rocks in Kenya.

   Rocks helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. in groups, learners brainstorm the meaning of rocks and share in class,

2. learners are guided to use print with suitable font type, size, and contrast or braille media or digital resources with assistive technology to establish the classification of rocks (according to mode of formation and age), download images and display in class,

3. in groups, learners discuss the characteristics of rocks (igneous, metamorphic and sedimentary) and make presentations in class, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. in groups, learners brainstorm the meaning of rocks and share in class,
2. learners are guided to use print with suitable font type, size, and contrast or braille media or digital resources with assistive technology to establish the classification of rocks (according to mode of formation and age), download images and display in class,
3. in groups, learners discuss the characteristics of rocks (igneous, metamorphic and sedimentary) and make presentations in class, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Rocks together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to Learn: The skill of sharing learnt knowledge is promoted as the learners carry out research in the library on the

significance of rocks in Kenya and write an essay.

● Digital Literacy: The skill of interacting with technology is enhanced as the learner uses digital resources with assistive

technology to establish the classification of rocks (according to mode of formation and age), download images and display

in class.

● Communication and collaboration: learners enhance listening, speaking, writing, reading and teamwork skills as they carry

out field study on rocks within the local environment, collect, classify and display the samples in class.

17

Values:
● Patriotism: Learner shows citizenship as they draw/describe tactile sketch maps of Kenya showing the distribution of rocks

● Unity: Learner embraces each other as they carry out field study on rocks within the local environment

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Environmental Education: Learner discusses the characteristics of rocks and make presentations in class.

● Safety in class and school environment: Learner carries out field study on rocks within the local environment, collects,

classifies and display the samples in class.

● First Aid: Learner carries out field study on rocks within the local environment.

Suggested Resources

Photographs and Pictures, Local and extended environment, Maps, Realia, Manilla papers, Gunny bags, Cartons, Digital

devices with assistive technology, Charts, marker pens, Sawdust, Sand, Approved textbooks and other print or braille

materials, Library resources, Museums, Rock artefacts, Whiteboards and marker pens, Rock Display Case

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. examine the classification of rocks according to the mode of formation and age,
2. describe the distribution of rocks in Kenya,
3. analyse the significance of rocks in Kenya,
4. sample rock types in your locality,
5. appreciate the significance of rocks in Kenya.

Remember the key question: Why are there different types of rocks? 2. How can rocks be classified?
